title: Compass of Essential Meaning
subtitle: Twenty thousand words, placed by goodness, power and danger

intro.value: _Draft intro._ **Ousiometry** asks what the essential dimensions of meaning are. Building on the old valence–arousal–dominance idea, it scores every word along five axes — **goodness, power, aggression, danger, structure** — and finds that a few of them carry most of the signal. Here are ~20,000 words from the [GPADS lexicon](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18509376) plotted along the three primary axes.

steps.value: The whole galaxy — ~20,000 words placed by **goodness** (x), **power** (y) and **danger** (z), coloured from red (bad) to blue (good). Drag to rotate.
Project straight onto the **Goodness × Power** plane: the split between pleasant and unpleasant words, high and low agency.
Now the **Danger × Power** plane — the corner where dangerous, high-power words gather.
And the **Goodness × Danger** plane, before we lift back into the full 3D cloud.
In the older **valence–arousal–dominance** language, goodness is _valence_ and power is _dominance_ — here as an ordinary 2D scatter of **Dominance × Valence**.
Back to the full galaxy in three dimensions.

conclusion.value: _Draft conclusion._ Word scores from the ousiometric GPADS lexicon (Dodds), [DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18509376](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18509376).
